_help:
usage: graph-loader [-h] [--version]
                    {schema-example,validate-schema,start,stop,status,replay-dlq} ...

Neo4j Graph Loader CLI

positional arguments:
  {schema-example,validate-schema,start,stop,status,replay-dlq}
    schema-example      Print a bundled schema YAML
    validate-schema     Validate a schema without services
    start               Start the ingestion pipeline
    stop                Stop running ingestion containers
    status              Check pipeline status and lags
    replay-dlq          Read a DLQ topic and republish matching envelopes to their source topic

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --version             show program's version number and exit
_help.replay-dlq:
usage: graph-loader replay-dlq [-h] [--config CONFIG]
                               (--node-label NODE_LABEL | --edge-type EDGE_TYPE)
                               [--reason-code REASON_CODE] [--since SINCE] [--until UNTIL]
                               [--limit LIMIT] [--target-topic TARGET_TOPIC]
                               [--source-topic TOPIC] [--dlq-topic DLQ_TOPIC] [--parked]
                               [--dry-run]

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --config CONFIG       Path to schema YAML (default: bundled canonical schema)
  --node-label NODE_LABEL
                        Replay this node label's DLQ topic
  --edge-type EDGE_TYPE
                        Replay this relationship type's DLQ topic
  --reason-code REASON_CODE
                        Only replay envelopes with this exact reason_code
  --since SINCE         Only replay envelopes at or after this ISO-8601 timestamp
  --until UNTIL         Only replay envelopes at or before this ISO-8601 timestamp
  --limit LIMIT         Replay at most this many matching envelopes (not messages scanned)
  --target-topic TARGET_TOPIC
                        Republish destination (default: the entity's own source topic; for a
                        relationship type with several topics, each envelope's original_topic)
  --source-topic TOPIC  Only replay envelopes whose original_topic is TOPIC (repeatable); TOPIC
                        must be one of the entity's topics
  --dlq-topic DLQ_TOPIC
                        Override the DLQ topic to read (default: resolved from the entity's
                        dead_letter block, even if enabled=false -- so a backlog from before
                        switching back to the file sink stays replayable). Required if the entity
                        has no dead_letter block at all
  --parked              Replay from the entity's parking-lot topic instead of its ordinary DLQ
                        topic (P5-S4). Ignored when --dlq-topic is given. A replayed parked record
                        republishes onto the original entity topic and re-enters the pipeline with
                        a fresh attempt_count=0.
  --dry-run             Count and log matching envelopes without publishing anything
_help.schema-example:
usage: graph-loader schema-example [-h] [--name {default,social}]

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --name {default,social}
_help.start:
usage: graph-loader start [-h] [--config CONFIG] [--run-dir BASE] --mode {bulk,stream}
                          [--network NETWORK] [--skip-image-build] [--accept-former-dlq TOPIC]
                          [--accept-dlq-leftovers TYPE]
                          [--bulk-timeout-seconds BULK_TIMEOUT_SECONDS]
                          [--bulk-edge-overlap {labels,shared}] [--edge-classic] [--edge-leases]
                          [--bucket-lease-buckets LEASE_BUCKETS]
                          [--bucket-lease-outer-batch-size LEASE_OUTER_BATCH_SIZE]
                          [--bucket-lease-keyed-max-nodes LEASE_KEYED_MAX_NODES]
                          [--retry-consumer-replicas RETRY_CONSUMER_REPLICAS]
                          [--stream-clock-rotation] [--edge-plan [PLAN_FILE]]
                          [--plan-writers PLAN_WRITERS] [--plan-workers PLAN_WORKERS]
                          [--plan-buckets PLAN_BUCKETS] [--plan-hub-degree PLAN_HUB_DEGREE]
                          [--plan-chunk-rows PLAN_CHUNK_ROWS] [--plan-partitions PLAN_PARTITIONS]
                          [--plan-topic PLAN_TOPIC] [--plan-dir PLAN_DIR]
                          [--plan-memory-mb PLAN_MEMORY_MB] [--plan-spill-dir PLAN_SPILL_DIR]
                          [--replace-stale-plan-topic] [--keep-plan-topic]
                          [--node-replicas-min-records NODE_REPLICAS_MIN_RECORDS]
                          [--max-node-replicas MAX_NODE_REPLICAS]
                          [--max-concurrent-bulk-edges MAX_CONCURRENT_BULK_EDGES]
                          [--run-id RUN_ID] [--stream-group-member-wait-seconds S]

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --config CONFIG       Path to schema YAML (default: bundled canonical schema)
  --run-dir BASE        Create a private persistent attempt under BASE (default: OS temporary
                        directory)
  --mode {bulk,stream}  Ingestion mode
  --network NETWORK     Docker network for containers
  --skip-image-build    require compatible preloaded images; never pull (start never builds
                        images)
  --accept-former-dlq TOPIC
                        Start although TOPIC, a relationship type's former default DLQ name
                        (<topic>.dlq or <type>.dlq), still holds records -- e.g. a drained DLQ
                        kept for audit, or a topic another deployment owns. Repeatable. Deleting
                        the old topics is the expected step instead
  --accept-dlq-leftovers TYPE
                        Start although relationship type TYPE's parked-pair index still holds
                        records of a topic it no longer reads, or of a topic now bound to another
                        label pair (they park after max_retry_attempts, blocking records of the
                        same keys until then). Repeatable. Draining the DLQ with the previous
                        schema first is the expected step instead
  --bulk-timeout-seconds BULK_TIMEOUT_SECONDS
                        Maximum seconds for each bulk lifecycle stage; progress-based where stages
                        run long: node draining, waiting for the edge plan (planner heartbeat) and
                        the planned dispatch fail only after this many seconds without progress
  --bulk-edge-overlap {labels,shared}
                        bulk, classic mode only (ignored with a warning unless --edge-classic is
                        given; default: labels): 'labels' serializes edge types sharing an
                        endpoint label; 'shared' runs them concurrently under globally ordered
                        APOC node locks and also schedules python_apoc self-referencing edges
                        alongside them instead of in a final isolated phase
  --edge-classic        bulk only: use the classic per-type APOC-locked relationship loaders. This
                        is the one bulk mode that can wait on Neo4j locks. Without any of --edge-
                        plan, --edge-leases and --edge-classic, bulk uses planned mode (or the
                        lease mode when the schema enables relationship dead_letter)
  --edge-leases         bulk only: run a global bucket-lease coordinator so concurrent
                        relationship transactions are node-disjoint across all edge types and
                        containers (no Neo4j lock waits); implies --bulk-edge-overlap shared
  --bucket-lease-buckets LEASE_BUCKETS
                        with --edge-leases (bulk), or by default with --mode stream: stable
                        buckets per node label (default: 16)
  --bucket-lease-outer-batch-size LEASE_OUTER_BATCH_SIZE
                        with --edge-leases (bulk), or by default with --mode stream: edge outer
                        flush size, split into bucket cells (default: 32000; overrides
                        edge_unwind_batch_size)
  --bucket-lease-keyed-max-nodes LEASE_KEYED_MAX_NODES
                        with --edge-leases (bulk), or by default with --mode stream: endpoint
                        labels whose node topic holds at most this many records are leased per
                        node key instead of per hash bucket (default: 1000; 0 = never)
  --retry-consumer-replicas RETRY_CONSUMER_REPLICAS
                        --mode stream only (P5-S4): replica count for the fleet-wide DLQ retry
                        consumer, launched automatically once any edge type has DLQ routing
                        enabled (default: 1)
  --stream-clock-rotation
                        DEPRECATED, removed after one release: for --mode stream, use the legacy
                        global batch clock with rotating relationship scheduling instead of the
                        default bucket-lease fleet
  --edge-plan [PLAN_FILE]
                        bulk only: load every relationship as globally planned, node-disjoint
                        chunks (no Neo4j lock waits) with one dispatcher and a pool of --plan-
                        writers writers; a chunk runs only once both endpoint labels are loaded.
                        Without a file the loader plans from the schema's relationship topics (up
                        to the bulk boundary) while the nodes load; with a file it loads the plan
                        a producer wrote (waited for up to --bulk-timeout-seconds)
  --plan-writers PLAN_WRITERS
                        with --edge-plan: writer containers across all edge types (default: Neo4j
                        available processors + 2; 10 if the server cannot be probed; never more
                        than the plan's chunks)
  --plan-workers PLAN_WORKERS
                        with --edge-plan (no file): planner processes reading the edge topics
                        (default: min(4, CPUs))
  --plan-buckets PLAN_BUCKETS
                        with --edge-plan (no file): hash buckets per node label (default:
                        clamp(writers, 8, 64), at most isqrt(records / (edge types * 500)), at
                        least 2)
  --plan-hub-degree PLAN_HUB_DEGREE
                        with --edge-plan (no file): nodes with at least this total degree over all
                        edge types get their own resource (default: the chunk size; 0 disables
                        hubs)
  --plan-chunk-rows PLAN_CHUNK_ROWS
                        with --edge-plan (no file): maximum rows per chunk transaction (default:
                        clamp(records / (20 * writers), 500, 5000))
  --plan-partitions PLAN_PARTITIONS
                        with --edge-plan (no file): partitions of the run's chunk topic (default:
                        4)
  --plan-topic PLAN_TOPIC
                        with --edge-plan (no file): new chunk topic to create (default: graph-
                        loader-edge-chunks-<run id>)
  --plan-dir PLAN_DIR   with --edge-plan (no file): directory for the plan file and its completion
                        ledger (default: private attempt plans directory)
  --plan-memory-mb PLAN_MEMORY_MB
                        with --edge-plan (no file): memory budget of each planner process in MiB
                        for buffered relationship rows, endpoint keys and Kafka queues; beyond it
                        the planner spills to --plan-spill-dir, so inputs far larger than RAM plan
                        with bounded memory (default: a quarter of the available RAM over the
                        planner processes, 256-4096 MiB)
  --plan-spill-dir PLAN_SPILL_DIR
                        with --edge-plan (no file): directory for the planner's temporary spill
                        files, removed after workers reap; needs about the relationship topics'
                        uncompressed size free (default: private attempt spill directory)
  --replace-stale-plan-topic
                        with --edge-plan (no file) and an explicit --run-id: delete the run's
                        chunk topic left behind by a killed run with the same run id, provided no
                        container of that run is alive (default: refuse to start, since the topic
                        may still be in use)
  --keep-plan-topic     with --edge-plan (no file): keep the run's chunk topic afterwards
                        (default: delete it)
  --node-replicas-min-records NODE_REPLICAS_MIN_RECORDS
                        bulk only: a node label whose YAML omits 'replicas' gets one loader when
                        its topic retains fewer records, else one per topic partition up to --max-
                        node-replicas (default: 10000; 0 = always the YAML value)
  --max-node-replicas MAX_NODE_REPLICAS
                        bulk only: cap for derived node-loader replicas (default: 8)
  --max-concurrent-bulk-edges MAX_CONCURRENT_BULK_EDGES
                        bulk, classic mode only (ignored with a warning unless --edge-classic is
                        given): maximum concurrently running shared edge types (0 = unlimited, the
                        default)
  --run-id RUN_ID       optional validated run identity. Names the run and scopes bulk
                        relationship consumer groups, container names and labels, the plan topic
                        and the lease server. Stream consumer groups are stable and do not use it,
                        except for one-time legacy offset migration
  --stream-group-member-wait-seconds S
                        stream mode: how long to wait for a stable consumer group's members to
                        expire before refusing to start (default: loading.session_timeout_ms + 5
                        s; a member that died during a rebalance can stay up to
                        max_poll_interval_ms + session_timeout_ms)
